newsitem.title: UK: Camelot to link up with Freemans - report.
newsitem.headline: Camelot to link up with Freemans - report.

text.p: British lottery operator Camelot is joining forces with the Freemans mail-order catalogue company, owned by Sears Plc, to boost ticket sales, the Times reported on Wednesday.
Freemans shoppers will receive a free lottery ticket for every 10 pounds sterling spent, the newspaper said. Tickets usually cost one pound each.
Camelot will receive 50 percent of all income from the deal after costs, with the rest going to charity, the paper said.
The report, which did not cite sources, said Freemans would pay an undisclosed partnership fee for the two-year arrangement, which begins in January.
Camelot is jointly owned by Cadbury Schweppes Plc, De La Rue Plc, GTECH UK, Racal Electronics Plc and ICL.
